quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: This white sign means you should not pass other vehicles:

options.text: Until after you pass the sign.
Unless it seems safe to do so.
For any reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: For any reason.
questions.explanation: A white rectangular sign is a mandatory rule. This sign means you cannot pass other vehicles under any circumstances.

questions.question: Trucks' blind spots are:

options.text: Directly behind the body.
On the immediate left of the cab.
Both on the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both on the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the body.
questions.explanation: Trucks have much larger blind spots than cars. The driver cannot see behind their vehicle. If you are driving behind or to the side of a truck, and you cannot see the driver's face in their mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, you should:

options.text: Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.
Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Drive closely to the parked vehicles to allow more room for moving traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your car and parked vehicles. A person may step out suddenly or a driver may start moving without seeing you.

questions.question: Vehicles stopped behind a school bus with its red lights flashing must remain stopped until:

options.text: All students are off the bus.
The stop arm is retracted.
The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stop arm is retracted and the bus resumes motion.
questions.explanation: When a school bus flashes red lights with its stop arm extended, you must stay stopped until the lights turn off, the arm pulls in, and the bus starts moving.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:

options.text: Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.
Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a full stop, check for other traffic and pedestrians, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving on the highway, consistently looking far ahead of your vehicle:

options.text: Helps you keep up with traffic.
Reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning.
Allows you to spot upcoming police officers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduces the need for last-minute braking or turning.
questions.explanation: Looking ahead lets you see problems early and react before you need to brake or swerve suddenly. This makes driving safer, saves fuel, and keeps traffic moving smoothly.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Crossroad ahead.
Merge.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Crossroad ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming ahead.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and maintain your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs warn of construction. Slow down and be ready to stop or avoid workers and equipment ahead.

questions.question: What message will be found on a red octagon-shaped sign?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An octagon-shaped sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway. The vehicle in front of you is a large truck. You should drive:

options.text: Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead than you can.
Farther behind the truck than you would when following a passenger vehicle.
No more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would when following a passenger vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely behind a truck, the driver cannot see you in their mirrors and does not know you are there. Tailgating is dangerous because you lose your safety cushion if the truck stops suddenly.

questions.question: What does alcohol affect first?

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol reduces your ability to drive safely. It goes from your stomach to your blood and then to all parts of your body. Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and driving skills.

questions.question: If a car is about to hit you from behind, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head firmly against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If your car is hit from behind, your body will move backward. Press yourself against your seat and push your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake to avoid hitting another vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Any prescription drug is safe if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
questions.explanation: Prescription and over-the-counter drugs can affect your ability to drive. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, or to calm nerves. It is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug—legal or illegal.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to all vehicles coming toward them. This includes bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: On a freeway, you should look farther ahead than on a city street to:

options.text: See hazards early.
Know that it takes a quarter mile to stop your vehicle.
Keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: See hazards early.
questions.explanation: On the freeway, watch for changes in traffic. Look for signals from other drivers. Expect vehicles merging at on-ramps and be ready for quick changes in road conditions and traffic flow.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: When driving in fog, slow down and use your low beam headlights. If you cannot see ahead, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: Should you drive on the shoulder to pass a car?

options.text: Yes, if the vehicle ahead is turning left.
No, never.
Yes, if the shoulder is wide enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: You can pass on the right only if you can do so without leaving the roadway. Never pass on the shoulder. The other driver will not expect you there and may pull onto the road.

questions.question: What color and shape are construction zone signs?

options.text: Square or rectangular, white and red.
Round or octagonal, black and yellow.
Diamond-shaped or rectangular, orange and black.

questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond-shaped or rectangular, orange and black.
questions.explanation: All temporary signs in work zones have an orange background with black letters or symbols. These signs appear on the right side of the road, or on both sides of a divided highway.

questions.question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal alcohol limit, your driving is not impaired.
Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. Good judgment helps you react safely to what you see and hear on the road. Even if you are below the legal limit, any alcohol reduces your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and can't find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car or other property, leave a note securely on the vehicle with your name, phone number, and address.

questions.question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:

options.text: Be able to safely drive at higher speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: To drive safely on the interstate, you must stay alert and be able to drive at high speeds.

questions.question: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit on primary and secondary state and federal highways is:

options.text: 55 mph.
45 mph.
65 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 55 mph.
questions.explanation: The default speed limit on primary and secondary state and federal highways is 55 miles per hour unless a different speed limit is posted.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
You should always brake hard to ensure stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply the brakes gently with increasing pressure so your vehicle stops smoothly.

questions.question: You have stopped for a train at a railroad crossing. After the train passes, you should:

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.
Look for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not proceed until all gates are lifted and all warning signals have stopped flashing.

questions.question: Water on the road can cause hydroplaning. Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:

options.text: 45 miles per hour.
35 miles per hour.
40 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 miles per hour.
questions.explanation: At speeds above 35 mph, tires cannot channel water away from the road. Your tires may lose contact with the road and ride over the water like skis.

questions.question: You must show proof of insurance to law enforcement:

options.text: Only if you are involved in a collision.
If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.
Only if you are stopped and cited.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.
questions.explanation: You must have proof of insurance with you when you drive. Show your proof of insurance and license to an officer after any traffic stop or collision.

questions.question: You can drive off the road to pass another vehicle:

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If there are two or more lanes traveling in your direction.
Under no circumstances.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under no circumstances.
questions.explanation: Never drive off the paved road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: While driving at night, a vehicle coming toward you has its high beams on, making it hard to see. You should:

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line indicates that passing is:

options.text: Permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.
Not permitted from either direction.
Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, passing is allowed from the side with the broken line and not allowed from the side with the solid line.

questions.question: At dawn or dusk and in rain or snow, it can be hard to see and be seen. A good way to let other drivers know you are there is to turn:

options.text: Up the dashboard lights.
On your parking lights.
On your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: On your headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly or when other drivers may have trouble seeing you. Use your low beam headlights whenever you need to use your windshield wipers.
